title: Accompanying Billie Holiday in Holiday on Broadway
summary: Stewart's trio with Billy Taylor accompanied Holiday in a mid-'40s Broadway show; he found her reserved, in good shape, and sees Lester Young's influence.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Billie Holiday as the musicians knew her

blocks.x: Now, did you ever work with Billy Holiday?
Billy Holiday? Yes. I worked in a show, a Broadway show, called "Holiday on Broadway."
Oh, and you played bass with her?
I played bass with Billy Taylor. He was with my trio at that time and a drummer.
Uh-huh. And did you all accompany her or --
We accompanied her on a couple of
numbers, yes.
What kind of a -- how long did the show go on?
I imagine -- let's see if I can remember. The show went on for, oh, about an hour and a half to --
No, I mean, how long did it run?
Oh, it ran, I'd say about a couple of weeks.
Oh, it was a couple of weeks on Broadway, huh?
Yeah. It moved around and moved to Boston and I think we went to Philadelphia for a couple of weeks.
And this was in the mid-'40s?
The mid-'40s, I believe.
How was the -- attendance must have been pretty good on Broadway if it stayed there for two weeks.
Yes, it was very good.
What kind of shape was she in at this time? Was she in good shape?
She was in very good shape, yes.
So a lot of the problems that she was later to have, she --
I know, yes.
-- seemed that she -- so she seemed in pretty -- she was in control of the stuff at that --
She was in control, yes.
She was singing well?
She was singing very well.
Uh-huh. But did you get to know her very well or did you over the years --

Well, fairly well because when I was working at the Three Deuces, she would be on at one time that same year. But she was appearing before she went on this show, this Broadway, "Holiday on Broadway," she was appearing at the Famous Door, which was right next to the Three Deuces. She appeared there with Count Basie's band, what have you, Lester Young was on the scene there with Count Basie.
What kind of a woman did she strike you as, as a personality?
Well, I didn't know her too well, of course. She was a lovely woman. She -- I don't know. Somehow, it seemed to me, she kept to herself quite a bit.
She was kind of reserved?
Reserved, yes.
Kind of like you said about Lester Young.
Yeah, right, right.
Maybe like a -- do you mean like a female version of that? Not so much, you know, I don't mean that she was imitating him or something, but --
I understand. She was real reserved. She didn't have too much to say.
But did she have a big sound when she sang or did she have a small sound?
I'd say in between.
Kind of a medium.
Yeah.
Wasn't real big.
A floating style to her singing. I don't know exactly how to explain it. It was very pleasing, yeah.
When you were playing with her, did she remind you at all of Lester Young in a way?
Yes, she did. In fact, I think that Lester Young was a big influence in the way she sang.
Yeah, that kind of flowing --
Flowing, yes.
